label: cli-deepseek-harness is a first-class executor kind (EXECUTOR_KINDS, LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS, EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT, hub mode) but has no if_cli_deepseek_harness single-executor branch in any of the four deep workflow YAMLs; its only trace is a notes bullet nested inside the if_cli_pi branch at deep-research-auto.yaml:1579 and deep-review-auto.yaml:2047 that asserts a single-executor path exists. A run whose config.executor.type is cli-deepseek-harness matches no branch and falls through to native, the exact silent-degrade failure the branch bodies document at deep-research-auto.yaml:1489 and that v4.0.0.0.md:127 promised closed.

The test 'fanout-run.cjs - unpinned lineage fallbacks match their packets' (fanout-run.vitest.ts:1774) enumerates six kinds and omits DSH_DEFAULT_MODEL, and cli-deepseek-harness publishes no 'Fan-out fallback:' line while the other six packets do (cli-pi in ROUTER.md:59, cli-devin in SKILL.md:146). The guard v4.0.0.16 hardened therefore has a hole exactly where the newest executor kind was added, and nothing fails to report it.
verify: grep -rn 'Fan-out fallback:' .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/*/SKILL.md .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/*/ROUTER.md  # 6 hits, none for cli-deepseek-harness

label: if_cli_copilot exists in deep-review-auto.yaml:1239, deep-review-confirm.yaml:1317 and deep-research-confirm.yaml:1190 but cli-copilot is neither an EXECUTOR_KINDS member nor a mode-registry mode, and the branch body concedes it at deep-review-auto.yaml:1288. It is unreachable via config.executor.type, and its presence makes deep-review-auto.yaml carry seven if_cli_* branches for seven CLI kinds so a count-based parity check passes while the sets differ by one in each direction. Removing it breaks nothing that dispatches; the review 16 KB @path behaviour in deep-review/changelog/v1.7.0.0.md:21 would need a live branch or retirement.

A ~100-line dispatch body is copied verbatim into the cursor, devin and pi single-executor branches, carrying the comment 'cursor-agent/devin/pi have no single-executor branch of their own' in all three copies (deep-research-auto.yaml:1287, :1388, :1489; deep-review-auto.yaml:1755, :1856, :1957). The literal claim is contradicted by the enclosing branches, and the triplication is the mechanism that produced f-iter001-001: a fourth kind needing the same body got no fourth copy, and any future fix must land three times or silently land once.
verify: grep -c 'no single-executor branch of their own' .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml  # 3

label: record_executor_audit is written as a sibling of the if_cli_* branches, so its position decides when the executor block is recorded relative to the dispatch it describes: at deep-research-auto.yaml:1580 it lands after the cursor/devin/pi branches and before the opencode/codex branches, and at deep-review-auto.yaml:2096 it lands after all of them. Cursor/devin/pi runs therefore record after dispatch while opencode/codex runs record before. Harmless today because the value is config-derived, but the ordering is accidental and any future move to record dispatch outcome there would record it for the wrong half of the kinds.

cli-devin publishes a hand-written-dispatch default of 'swe' (SKILL.md:100) and a fan-out fallback of SWE 2 Max (SKILL.md:146); cli-claude-code publishes claude-sonnet-5-5 (SKILL.md:106) against an Opus fallback (SKILL.md:108). Both lines are correct in their own context and the split is deliberate and test-enforced, but neither line names the context it governs, so an operator who reads 'Default model' and omits --model gets a different model than an unpinned lineage. The split is explained only in a runner source comment the operator will not read.

v4.0.0.0.md:125 states Cursor carries 21 ids across six families and Pi runs a closed six-provider roster; the tree holds 29 Cursor ids (executor-config.ts:353) and 10 Pi ids (executor-config.ts:222). Growth within a release line is expected, but no later note in v4.0.0.x, v4.0.1.0 or v4.0.2.0 restates the rosters, so the stale numbers are the only roster summary a changelog reader finds.

v4.0.0.0.md:48 names the seven bridges as 'Cursor and Hermes join OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Devin and Pi'; v4.0.2.0.md:160 removes Hermes and adds DeepSeek Harness. The cardinality stayed at seven, so every assertion of 'seven bridges' - including the registry prose 'All seven modes route by hub membership' at mode-registry.json:8 - passes while the set it names is different. Membership, not count, is the property worth asserting.

The four enforced model allowlists and their defaults, duplicated between executor-config.ts constants and fanout-run.cjs synchronous copies, are in exact parity: pi 10 ids, cursor 29, devin 23, dsh 2, empty symmetric difference, identical defaults. Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode carry no allowlist in either file by design, with defaults single-sourced in the runner (gpt-6-luna, claude-opus-4-8, llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017). EXECUTOR_KINDS, EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT and LINEAGE_COMMAND_ADAPTERS are also in tri-parity for all eight kinds. Parity failure in this cluster lives at the workflow layer, not the runtime layer.

direction: Treating the cli-devin 'swe' vs 'swe-2-max' and cli-claude-code sonnet vs opus default-model split as code/prose drift
reason: fanout-run.cjs:2596 states the runner defaults are deliberately not the hand-written-dispatch recommendation, and fanout-run.vitest.ts:1774 enforces family equality against each packet's dedicated 'Fan-out fallback:' line. The divergence is context-scoped by design; the real defect is that the packets do not name the context (f-iter001-006).

label: The append gateway accepts a full iteration record (runId, sessionId, lineageId, focus, mode, target_agent, answeredQuestions) and the canonical state-log row it refreshes carries only seven fields: type, iteration, run, status, newInfoRatio, ruledOut, timestamp. The projection is the deep_research.iteration_completed branch at deep-research-contract.ts:297, which reads status, rawNewInfoRatio and ruledOutApproachRefs and emits nothing else. The prompt-pack contract makes answeredQuestions mandatory and says the reducer ticks a strategy box only on an exact text match, so a consumer reading the state log - which the contract calls the canonical record - sees no answered question and no run identity. The reducer survives only because it also reads the delta files, where the full record is intact.

direction: Re-spending effort on whether the duplicated allowlists have drifted apart
reason: Programmatic set comparison over both source texts returns an empty symmetric difference for all four enforced kinds. Recorded as inv-iter001-001 so later iterations treat it as settled.
